chunk_findings.detail: `_queue` maps *every* unsuccessful invocation — network failure, expired/insufficient auth, 403/429 rate limit, GitHub 5xx, or an Enterprise schema that rejects the query — onto the exact same value it uses for a definite negative ("this PR has no merge-queue entry"). The docstring only justifies that mapping for forges that genuinely have no merge queue ("answers 'not queued', which is what it is"); it says nothing about transient errors, which on a queue-enabled repo are indistinguishable from "not queued" and therefore lie. The consequence is concrete because of the intent stated for this change: `pr sync` treats an open request that was queued and no longer is as `queue_ejected`, and the whole point of reading the queue is that a queued request is never re-merged. Concretely: PR #7 is sitting in the queue at position 2; one poll of `_info` hits a rate limit and `gh api graphql` exits 1 ("API rate limit exceeded") → `returncode != 0` → `("", 0, "")` → `info.queue == ""` → the sync announces `queue_ejected` for a PR that is still queued and (believing nothing is queued) is free to issue another `gh pr merge`. This is not a rare corner: `_queue` is invoked once per open PR on every `_info`, so the added GraphQL traffic itself makes hitting the rate limit more likely. Either return an "unknown" sentinel distinct from `""` (or keep the previous value) on failure, or only treat a successful GraphQL response as authoritative.

chunk_findings.detail: The new annotation gates on `r.get("queue")` but then interpolates `r['queue_position']` unconditionally. The rest of this change explicitly treats the position as possibly absent: `_queue_detail` in `ddflow/services/flow.py` renders `"position unknown"` when `info.queue_position` is falsy, and `_report_queue`/`_waiting` both propagate a queue entry with no position as `None`. So for a queued PR with an unknown position (the case the fakeforge's new merge queue can produce), `r.get("queue")` is truthy, the branch is taken, and `pr status` prints `[merge queue #None]` rather than a skipped/"unknown" marker; and if a row ever carries `queue` without a `queue_position` key it raises `KeyError` instead of degrading. The condition should test the position (e.g. `r.get("queue_position")`) or format it with a fallback, matching how `_queue_detail` handles the same value.

chunk_findings.detail: `_queue` maps *every* failure of the single `gh api graphql` call — non-zero exit (rate limiting/secondary limits, 5xx on api.github.com, expired token scope, `gh` transient failure) as well as a malformed/error payload (`{"errors":[...],"data":null}` is HTTP 200 and lands in the `TypeError` handler) — to the exact same `("", 0, "")` it returns for "this PR is not in the merge queue". But the contract defined for the same field in this very diff (`PRInfo.queue`: "An open request that WAS queued and no longer is, was ejected") says that state on an open request means *ejected*. Concrete scenario: PR #7 is reported queued at position 2, so the previous sync recorded `queue="queued"`; on the next sync the single `gh api graphql` call for #7 hits the API rate limit and exits non-zero, `_queue` returns `("", 0, "")`, and pr sync sees "was queued, now not, still open" → reports `queue_ejected` for a request that is in fact still sitting in the queue. Given the stated intent this path can then re-merge/re-enqueue the request. The "best effort" fallback is only safe for "this forge has no merge-queue field"; conflating it with "the query did not complete" is what makes a transient environment failure indistinguishable from a real dequeue.

The consequence is concrete because of the intent stated for this change: `pr sync` treats an open request that was queued and no longer is as `queue_ejected`, and the whole point of reading the queue is that a queued request is never re-merged. This is not a rare corner: `_queue` is invoked once per open PR on every `_info`, so the added GraphQL traffic itself makes hitting the rate limit more likely. Either return an "unknown" sentinel distinct from `""` (or keep the previous value) on failure, or only treat a successful GraphQL response as authoritative.
